prime.options.screenshot_mode.tooltip: Freezes the current camera, sun, terrain, and animated block textures, then accumulates unbiased path-traced samples at native resolution. This completely bypasses DLSS RR, NRD, FSR, and all realtime debug overlays. Press Ctrl+Alt+F2 to enter or exit without affecting ordinary F2 screenshots; Escape only exits and never enters. This setting lasts only for the current game session.
prime.options.fsr.quality.tooltip: FSR (FidelityFX Super Resolution) path traces at a lower internal resolution and reconstructs the image at the window resolution. Higher quality preserves distant detail; higher performance usually improves frame rate. For a 4K display, start with Quality and lower it only when more performance is needed.
prime.options.post_processing.mode.toolt: Selects the complete realtime post-processing path. Supported RTX devices default to DLSS RR; unavailable or failed RR sessions fall back to NRD-FSR. Disabled presents native-resolution 1 spp noise directly and is intended only for inspecting the integrator. Reference screenshots are independent of this option.
prime.options.post_processing.quality.to: Controls the internal path-tracing resolution. NRD-FSR uses its established ratios; DLSS RR queries NVIDIA's recommended dimensions; disabled post-processing always renders at native resolution.
prime.options.dlss_rr.debug_view.tooltip: Visualizes the exact images Prime submits to DLSS Ray Reconstruction. HDR colors use the common display transform while numeric guides use meaning-preserving mappings. It is available only while RR is active, does not reset history, and is never written to the config file.
prime.options.dlss_rr.debug_fullscreen.t: Shows the selected RR diagnostic across the screen instead of as a panel in the upper-right corner. This temporary state is never written to the config file.
prime.options.lighting.sun_ev.tooltip: Exposure value (EV) changes direct sunlight, the sky, and atmospheric scattering together. Each step is 0.25 EV; adding 1 EV doubles brightness. Start with the default 0 EV and adjust it only when the whole outdoor scene looks too bright or too dark.
prime.options.lighting.block_light_ev.to: Exposure value (EV) changes illumination from emissive blocks such as torches and glowstone without changing which blocks emit light. Each step is 0.25 EV; adding 1 EV doubles brightness. Start with the default 0 EV.
prime.options.display.oklab_overexposure: Highlight overexposure controls how much brightness headroom the Oklab display transform gives to bright areas without changing the scene's physical lighting. Higher values make the sun, lamps, and reflections brighter; excessive values can wash out detail. Start at the calibrated default of 1.15625× and adjust only when highlights look overly compressed or bright.
prime.options.material.default_roughness: Roughness controls whether highlights are sharp or spread out and applies only to blocks without a PBR roughness texture. Lower values look smoother with tighter reflections; higher values look rougher with softer highlights. It never overrides roughness explicitly supplied by a resource pack. Keep the default 0.80 unless ordinary blocks look broadly too glossy or too matte.
prime.options.nrd.debug_view.tooltip: Presents NRD's native validation output with nearest-neighbor scaling, bypassing FSR and the Oklab display transform so diagnostic colors and relationships remain intact. Switching it does not reset history and it is never written to the config file.
prime.options.fsr.debug_view.tooltip: Presents FidelityFX FSR's native integration overview while bypassing the Oklab display transform, preserving its labels, colors, and numeric range. Switching it does not reset history and it is never written to the config file.
